newsitem.title: FRANCE: RsF appeals to Menem over photographer's murder.
newsitem.headline: RsF appeals to Menem over photographer's murder.

text.p: An international press freedom watchdog on Thursday urged Argentine President Carlos Menem to speed up the probe into the murder of a news photographer.

"As long as investigators fail to identify and detain those who carried out and ordered the murder, the assassination of Jose Luis Cabezas will remain as a tragic sign of deteriorating press freedom in Argentina," Reporters without Borders (RsF) told Menem in a letter released to the press.
The Paris-based group praised Menem's pledge to punish the murderers, but it added it was concerned about the conditions in which the investigation was being carried out.
RsF also voiced concern over threats made over the past two weeks against 12 journalists, some of whom had taken part in protests against Cabezas' murder.
Cabezas was shot and his handcuffed body incinerated in his car on January 25. The crime revived grim memories of the political violence which rocked Argentina during military rule in the 1970s.
The investigation has been marred by allegations of police inefficiency, but there have been recent signs of progress in the probe.
